newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Indonesia JV in $950 mln petrochem project funding.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia JV in $950 mln petrochem project funding.

text.p: PT Trans-Pacific Petrochemical Indotama (TPPI) has signed a pact with seven banks to arrange and underwrite a US$950 million project financing, financial advisor BA Asia said on Tuesday.
TPPI is an Indonesian petrochemical joint venture company.
The US$950 million financing is the portion of overall funding allocated to international commercial banks for TPPI's planned US$2.3 billion olefins and aromatics complex near Tuban, East Java.

Shareholders of TPPI are PT Tirtamas Majutama with 10 percent, Trans Pacific Petrochemicals Ltd (an affiliate of Tirtamas) with 60 percent, Tuban Petochemicals Ptd Ltd (a subsidiary of Siam Cement Public Co Ltd ) with 20 percent, Nissho Iwai Corp with five percent and Itochu Corp with five percent.

BA Asia, Banque Nationale de Paris, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (Singapore), DKB Merchant Bank (Singapore), Fuji Bank, Sanwa Bank and Societe Generale Asia are the seven lead arrangers. Each will underwrite US$135.71 million.
The US$950 million in project debt provided by the international commercial banks respresents the majority of the overall US$1.725 billion in debt required for the project.
A significant portion of the US$950 million financing will be supported by export credit agencies, including the U.S. Export-Import Bank and the Export Credit Guarantee Department (ECGD).
The balance of the financing has been allocated to other export credit agencies, including the Export-Import Bank of Japan (JEXIM), to Japanese trading companies and to Indonesian banks.
The project is scheduled for completion in mid-1999.
When completed, the TPPI complex will be Indonesia's first integrated olefins and aromatics facility.
